key_insight: Suvorexant increased the phosphorylated-to-unphosphorylated tau-181 ratio in plasma while decreasing it in cerebrospinal fluid, showing opposite biomarker responses across compartments.
clinical_relevance: Medication-related changes in plasma tau biomarkers may complicate their interpretation for Alzheimer disease screening and trial enrollment.
method: Secondary analysis of a randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving 25 participants receiving placebo or suvorexant 20 mg.
Longitudinal paired cerebrospinal fluid and plasma sampling via indwelling catheters.
Mass spectrometry for plasma Alzheimer biomarkers and SomaScan 11K proteomics at hours 0, 16, and 24.
evidence_signal: Opposite plasma and cerebrospinal fluid pT181/T181 changes occurred between 08:00 and 16:00, alongside proteomic pathway shifts centrally at 16 hours and peripherally at 24 hours.
watch_item: This small, acute secondary analysis does not establish long-term effects on Alzheimer disease progression or clinical benefit.
paper_title: Suvorexant Inversely Affects Phosphorylated Tau in Human Cerebrospinal Fluid and Plasma
